items.prompt: Why compare a PCA axis projector instead of a hardcoded eigenvector sign?

options.text: The sign proves whether a factor is profitable
options.why: Axis sign is a coordinate convention, not economic evidence.

options.text: Eigenvectors must always contain exactly the same bits
options.why: Numerical bases and signs can vary.

options.text: v and -v define the same axis/projector
options.why: Their scores flip but reconstructed projection is unchanged.

options.text: Repeated eigenvalues identify a unique coordinate axis
options.why: Any orthonormal basis in the repeated eigenspace is valid.

items.explanation: Projector/subspace comparisons respect the mathematical ambiguity that componentwise sign assertions ignore.
